Rather than reproducing an identical 77.10% across all three algorithms, the agent's from-scratch evaluation shows that `rel-att` and `grad-att` yield the same answer on 87–91% of questions while unsmoothed `pure-grad` (78.6%, 42% hit rate) merely captures the random-zoom effect, offering a more rigorous mechanistic test of zoom versus attention strategy than the paper's speculation. However, the score is tempered because Qwen2.5-VL was artificially capped at a 448x448 pixel budget on a 200-sample CPU subset rather than evaluated at native dynamic resolution, `pure-grad` omitted smoothing heuristics, and the paper's points regarding baseline margin compression and third-party PR modularity are absent.
